rule: MoPH pays 100% of emergency care and of a defined list of hospital admissions for every uninsured Lebanese citizen, displaced or not.
who_is_eligible: Lebanese citizens with no other insurer (no NSSF, army, private insurance, etc.)
where: All government hospitals + private hospitals that accepted the MoPH 'fair treatment ceiling' (list attached to the source page)
comment: Supersedes 2026-03-03 war-time 100% rule (82829) and the 2026-01-30 rule that normal coverage is 80% with 100% only for border-village displaced (82424).

rule: The 100% coverage covers all emergency cases plus a specific set of hospitalization cases, not every admission.
comment: Which admissions are covered is not listed on the page; ask 1787 or check the attached hospital list/decision.

rule: Normal MoPH coverage in government hospitals is 80%; patients displaced from front-line border villages get 100% for hospitalization and 300+ ministry-defined operations by showing papers issued through their municipality.
who_is_eligible: Uninsured Lebanese displaced from southern border villages (registered with Ministry of Social Affairs)
comment: Probably overtaken by the 2026-07-02 statement that all uninsured Lebanese get 100% (85973). Keep for the 80% baseline. Circular PDF: /userfiles/files/laws/letter26-1-3165.pdf (item 82443).

rule: Government hospitals and the listed private hospitals must apply the 100% hospitalization and emergency coverage and may not charge patients any price difference; patients should report demands for money to hotline 1787.
where: Government hospitals + private hospitals listed in the circular
comment: Circular PDF attached on source page.

rule: MoPH and the Syndicate of Hospitals agreed on joint follow-up to stop hospitals collecting extra payments from patients contrary to the law.
The minister stated that hospitals will not be allowed to refuse to admit emergency cases.
comment: The brief mentions a 6 Sep 2026 rule that hospitals must admit emergency surgery at MoPH expense; the only 6 Sep source found is this TV interview. Verify against the Laws/circulars section after the full crawl.

rule: Lebanese law obliges medical institutions to receive necessary medical cases (explained in the free guide 'Know your rights in health').
comment: Guide PDF: /userfiles/files/Publications/Free Guide -Know Your Health Rights/ (attached to source).

rule: During the war MoPH treats the wounded at its own expense in government and private hospitals, insured or not, and pays a lump sum for emergency-room care of wounded who are not admitted.
comment: War-period measure; confirm it is still active.

rule: Organ transplants (heart, kidney, liver) are again performed at MoPH expense; a national committee is drafting the implementing decrees for organ donation.
where: Transplant-capable hospitals (e.g. Al-Rassoul Al-Aazam, St George University Hospital)
comment: Transplants had stopped for ~5 years before this.

rule: MoPH hospital coverage now includes bone-marrow transplants, kidney transplants and open-heart surgery.
comment: Earlier mention (kidney + bone marrow + glaucoma) on 2026-09-06 (86817).

rule: Glaucoma treatment has been added to MoPH hospital coverage (alongside kidney and bone-marrow transplants).
MoPH plans to add cochlear implants, scoliosis correction and cardiac pacemakers to coverage.
comment: Announcement of intent only. Do NOT tell patients these are covered yet.

rule: Stroke thrombectomy (catheter clot removal) is covered 100% at MoPH expense, including one ICU night.
who_is_eligible: Stroke patients who are MoPH beneficiaries
where: Reference stroke hospitals in the national stroke network

rule: Hip/pelvic fracture prostheses for the elderly are covered: 80% in government hospitals and 65% in private hospitals.
who_is_eligible: Elderly MoPH beneficiaries with hip/pelvic fractures

rule: Coverage was raised for 'second-category' patients, especially rehabilitation for paralysis and treatment of substance-use disorders.
MoPH pays USD 96 per hemodialysis session (doctor's fee included), so the patient should not pay anything extra.

Chronic hemodialysis patients register in the MoPH chronic renal failure registry (form HEA009): ID, 2 photos, residence certificate, lab tests (CBC, BUN, creatinine, electrolytes, Cl-cr, HCV, HIV, HBsAg, renal echo) and a monthly-sessions report signed by the doctor; submit Tuesdays and Thursdays.
who_is_eligible: Chronic kidney failure patients on hemodialysis
where: MoPH, Artificial Kidney section, Bir Hassan (Jnah, near Ogero)
comment: Service page, no date shown.

rule: 100% coverage applies to dialysis and chemotherapy patients wherever they are displaced.
comment: War-period statement; still consistent with the 2026-07-02 rule.

rule: Digital mammography is free all year round in every government hospital for Lebanese women over 40; positive cases are followed by PHC-centre doctors via the Phenix system.
comment: Replaces the old once-a-year October campaign model.

rule: People injured in the Beirut port explosion are treated 100% at MoPH expense for all related medical, surgical and hospital care, whatever their insurer; hospitals may not charge differences. Untreated injured should contact the Directorate of Medical Care at the main MoPH building.
where: All government hospitals; private hospitals already treating them
comment: Earlier statement 2026-08-05 (86468).

rule: 'Karim' initiative: families evacuated from collapsing buildings in Tripoli get 100% coverage in government hospitals and free consultations/tests at PHC centres using a health card.
who_is_eligible: Families from collapsing/evacuated buildings in Tripoli

rule: Cancer and intractable-disease medicines are collected at the MoPH Drug Dispensing Centre near Karantina Government Hospital, Mon–Fri 08:00–10:00. First time: a medicine file approved by the MoPH scientific committee + ID. Renewals: specialist prescription within one month of the last pickup + drug card + ID. Patient in person, or a relative, or a notarised proxy. Free, same day.
who_is_eligible: Patients with an approved MoPH medicine file

rule: To get MoPH medicine assistance, submit the disease-specific request form (e.g. Antineoplastic/NCR, Multiple Sclerosis, Bleeding Disorders, Iron overload, Kidney/organ transplantation, IBD, Rheumatic, Hepatitis, HIV, Psychotropic) with ID, detailed medical report and prescription. Patient must be Lebanese with no other insurer, and treatment must follow the Drugs National Guidelines. Takes about 2 weeks.
who_is_eligible: Lebanese patients with no other insurer
where: MoPH Directorate General of Health, Equipment & Supply Dept, Bir Hassan (Jnah, near Ogero); email drugs@moph.gov.lb
comment: Forms are downloadable from the service page (/AdministrativeServices/download/{id}).

rule: Cancer medicines: apply with the 'Antineoplastic Drugs / National Cancer Registry' form (adult or paediatric). Approved patients collect drugs at the Karantina Drug Dispensing Centre. Hotline 1214 handles cancer and intractable-disease medicines.
who_is_eligible: Lebanese cancer patients with no other insurer
comment: See also service 6 and hotline row 82895.

rule: Cancer patients obtain narcotic pain medicines with a medical report signed by two doctors (one the treating doctor), pathology result and civil-registry extract; max 5 injections/day (no limit stated for tablets/patches); prescription valid 7 days.
where: MoPH Pharmacy Service, Narcotics Dept, Bir Hassan

rule: Multiple sclerosis medicines are requested through the MoPH medicine-assistance form 'Multiple Sclerosis Therapy'.
who_is_eligible: Lebanese MS patients with no other insurer

rule: Bleeding-disorder (haemophilia/von Willebrand) medicines: form AK014BD-2 with ID, medical report, prescription, blood studies (CBC, platelets, PT, PTT, bleeding time) and exact factor dosages (VWF, VII, VIII, IX, fibrinogen).
who_is_eligible: Lebanese bleeding-disorder patients with no other insurer

rule: Iron-overload (chelation) medicines, as used in thalassaemia, are requested with form AK015Iron-2: ID, medical report, prescription and blood studies (CBC, ferritin, LFTs, BUN, Cr, Hb electrophoresis).
who_is_eligible: Lebanese patients with iron overload (e.g. thalassaemia) and no other insurer
comment: The site doesn't name thalassaemia explicitly; it is mapped to 'Iron overload'.

rule: Post-transplant medicines are requested with the form 'Transplantation Kidney or other Organs'; bone-marrow transplant has its own form.
who_is_eligible: Lebanese transplant patients with no other insurer

rule: Humira (adalimumab 40 mg SC) is on the MoPH AMAN list of intractable-disease medicines under 7 classes (IBD, Crohn's, ulcerative colitis, rheumatic, dermatological, uveitis, clinical immunology) and on the Tender 388/2024 free-distribution list; request it through the matching disease form.
who_is_eligible: Lebanese patients with no other insurer
comment: Linked from /ar/Pages/3/77224. Request route: service 1 (Rheumatic / IBD / Dermatological forms), pickup at Karantina (service 6).

rule: MoPH publishes three lists of medicines it distributes free: the allocation list, the Tender 388/2024 list, and the AMAN intractable-diseases list (Excel files).
comment: Parsed into data/structured/free_meds.csv.

rule: Displaced people can collect chronic and acute medicines free at primary health care centres, and PHC consultations are paid by MoPH; mobile clinics distribute medicines in shelters.
comment: War-period; see also 82895 (2026-03-07).

rule: UNHCR informed MoPH that it would stop covering hospitalization of displaced Syrians from November 2025.
comment: Check whether any later arrangement replaced it.

rule: 1787: MoPH hotline for hospitalization questions and complaints (including being asked to pay differences), mainly for displaced and uninsured patients; answered during working hours.
comment: On 2026-03-03 it was announced as 24/7 (82829). The newer page says working hours.

rule: 1214: MoPH hotline, also for cancer and intractable-disease medicines and for directing chemotherapy patients to treatment centres.
comment: Also shown in the site header on every page.

rule: 1564: mental health hotline for psychological support.
Ministerial decision 1/542 (26 Mar 2026) regulates selling certain E1 and E2 tier medicines in pharmacies.
comment: Details are in the attached decision; read it before summarising.

rule: MoPH announced the HPV vaccine would be added free for target groups in the national immunization programme.
comment: Announcement; confirm rollout.
